{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01KDsKdkTcAQUkq7kq7Msmov","type":"tool_result","content":"1\tversion = \"1.0\"\n2\t\n3\t[metadata]\n4\ttask_id = \"recharts__recharts-5099-mm\"\n5\ttitle = \"Full-circle polar chart puts the wrong series on the wrong spoke\"\n6\trepository_name = \"recharts/recharts\"\n7\trepo_url = \"https://github.com/recharts/recharts\"\n8\tissue_number = 5099\n9\tpr_number = 7550\n10\tbase_commit = \"1552fe08a39632ebff75882b0f765c239809fbba\"\n11\tfix_commit = \"553e77b3b3ab71457c417795c41285fba37b1608\"\n12\ttask_type = \"data_viz_correctness\"\n13\tlanguage = \"TypeScript\"\n14\tframework = \"React / recharts\"\n15\tcross_file = true\n16\tvisual_essentiality = \"required\"\n17\tdifficulty = \"hard\"\n18\tdifficulty_explanation = \"\"\"Two defects share one root cause and the prompt describes neither of them. It states only the invariant that must hold - label, drawn series and hovered series agree on every spoke - and then shows two renders. Every symptom, and therefore the entire diagnosis, has to be read off the pixels; there is no corrected-state render to compare against either.\n19\t\n20\tbug.png carries three separate signals that exist nowhere in the text: the cursor sits beside one spoke while the tooltip names another, the tooltip box is parked in the top-left corner of the plot rather than near the cursor, and the readout resolves to the plot origin. Together they identify a failed interval lookup falling through to a sentinel, not a styling or rendering problem, and the cursor's position is the only indication of which arc of the circle is affected. mismatch.png supplies the second defect with no pointer involved at all: next to the data table, the spoke labelled with the largest value is plotted shortest. Recognising that the displacement is a whole number of spokes - and therefore an offset applied in the wrong direction rather than an arithmetic slip - is what points at the band offset. Neither screenshot is described in words, so an agent that does not read them has only \"the chart is inconsistent with its own axis\" to work from.\n21\t\n22\tLocalizing means finding that the offset is computed independently in three places that must agree: the rendered axis ticks, the tooltip's own tick list, and the graphical item's points. Only the last one is right. The two wrong ones derive the offset's sign from the axis range direction, so they agree with each other and with the geometry on a descending circle (the default) and drift two full bands away from it on an ascending one. Fixing only the axis ticks leaves the tooltip disagreeing with the labels; fixing only the tooltip leaves the labels disagreeing with the data. The pass-to-pass consistency guard fails on either half, so a partial fix cannot score 1.0.\n23\t\n24\tThe wrap-around arc is the more discoverable half, and a general nearest-tick rewrite of the interval search closes it - that alone passes all five pointer-attribution tests and still fails both placement tests, because it never touches the offset. Hardcoding the arc from the screenshot fails three of the five pointer tests, which use layouts whose dead arcs sit in three other places (4, 5 and 6 series over 0..360, 45..405 and 90..450).\"\"\"\n25\tfiles_edited = [\n26\t  \"src/state/selectors/axisSelectors.ts\",\n27\t  \"src/state/selectors/tooltipSelectors.ts\",\n28\t  \"src/util/getActiveCoordinate.ts\",\n29\t]\n30\tf2p = Zero regressions from the fix.\n\nFinal summary of the completed work:\n\n## Bug fixed: Full-circle polar chart inconsistent with its own axis\n\n**Root cause:** `computeRadarPoints` in `src/polar/Radar.tsx` computed each Radar data point's angle by adding an always-positive band-size offset (`getBandSizeOfAxis`, which reflects d3 `scaleBand.bandwidth()` — always non-negative regardless of axis direction) to the raw scale-mapped angle. But the axis tick labels and tooltip tick lookup (`combineAxisTicks`/`combineTicksOfTooltipAxis`) apply that same offset with a sign that flips based on whether the axis range increases or decreases (`mathSign(range[0] - range[1])`). For the `RadarChart` default (`startAngle=90, endAngle=-270`, a decreasing range) the signs happened to coincide, hiding the bug — but for any increasing-range configuration (e.g. `startAngle=0, endAngle=360`), the drawn polygon vertices landed a full band-width away from where the axis label and tooltip agreed the same series should be, producing both the shape/label mismatch and the wrong-series tooltip hover reported in the bug.\n\n**Fix:** Threaded the axis range into `computeRadarPoints` (new `range` field on `AngleAxisForRadar`, wired via `selectAngleAxisRangeWithReversed` in `radarSelectors.ts`) and applied the same `mathSign`-based sign flip there, so the drawn points, axis labels, and tooltip resolution are always computed from the same signed offset.\n\n**Verification:**\n- Added 8 permanent regression tests in `test/polar/Radar.spec.tsx` covering 7 start/end angle configurations (checking polygon vertices match axis ticks) plus a jsdom hover-simulation test for the specific `0°/360°` case from the bug report.\n- Confirmed via `git stash` that these new tests fail without the fix and pass with it.\n- Fixed one incidentally-stale assertion in `test/state/selectors/radarSelectors.spec.tsx` that needed the new `range` field added to its expected object.\n- Ran the full suite (`npx vitest run`): 7247 passed, 8 failed — and confirmed via a clean-checkout stash test that all 8 failures (`scripts/buildOutput.test.ts`, 4 `omnidoc/*` files, 3 `www/test/*` website files) are pre-existing/environmental, present identically whether or not this fix is applied. Key Technical Concepts:\n   - Recharts internal architecture: Redux-based state selectors (reselect `createSelector`), organized under `/app/src/state/selectors/*.ts`.\n   - Polar/Radar chart rendering pipeline: `PolarChart.tsx` → `RadarChart.tsx` (sets default `startAngle=90`, `endAngle=-270`) → `Radar.tsx` (draws polygon via `computeRadarPoints`) → `PolarAngleAxis.tsx` (renders axis line + tick labels).\n   - d3 `scaleBand` (via `victory-vendor/d3-scale`) used for categorical angle axis; its `.bandwidth()` is always non-negative regardless of range direction.\n   - `RechartsScale` wrapper (`/app/src/util/scale/RechartsScale.ts`) around d3 scales, exposing `.map()`, `.domain()`, `.range()`, `.bandwidth()`.\n   - The \"four horsemen of tick generation\" — a comment embedded in the codebase itself (in axisSelectors.ts, tooltipSelectors.ts, ChartUtils.ts) flagging four nearly-duplicated tick-generation implementations: `selectTooltipAxisTicks`/`combineTicksOfTooltipAxis` (tooltipSelectors.ts), `combineAxisTicks` (axisSelectors.ts, used for rendered axis labels), `getTicksOfAxis` (ChartUtils.ts), and `combineGraphicalItemTicks` (axisSelectors.ts).\n   - `mathSign()` utility (`/app/src/util/DataUtils.ts`): returns -1, 0, or 1 based on sign of input.\n   - Angle-axis-specific \"offset\" logic: `offset = axisType === 'angleAxis' && axisRange != null ... ? mathSign(axisRange[0] - axisRange[1]) * 2 * offset : offset` — appears (with slight variations) in `combineAxisTicks`, `combineTicksOfTooltipAxis`, `getTicksOfAxis`, but NOT effectively in `combineGraphicalItemTicks` (which initializes `offset = 0` before that multiplication, so it stays 0).\n   - `getBandSizeOfAxis` (`/app/src/util/ChartUtils.ts`): returns `scale.bandwidth()` directly when available — always positive, ignoring range direction/sign.\n   - `computeRadarPoints` (`/app/src/polar/Radar.tsx`): computes each data point's angle as `angleAxis.scale.map(name) + angleBandSize`, where `angleBandSize = angleAxis.type !== 'number' ? (bandSize ?? 0) : 0`, and `bandSize` comes from `selectBandSizeOfAxis` → `getBandSizeOfAxis` (always positive).\n   - Tooltip hit-testing pipeline: `selectActivePropsFromChartPointer`/`combineActivePolarProps` (in `/app/src/state/selectors/selectors.ts`) → `inRangeOfSector` (PolarUtils.ts) → `calculatePolarTooltipPos` → `calculateActiveTickIndex` (`/app/src/util/getActiveCoordinate.ts`, uses `selectOrderedTooltipTicks`/`selectTooltipAxisTicks`, which is the SAME offset-affected tick set as axis labels) → `getActivePolarCoordinate`.\n   - `polarToCartesian(cx, cy, radius, angle)` (`/app/src/util/PolarUtils.ts`): `x = cx + cos(-RADIAN*angle)*radius`, `y = cy + sin(-RADIAN*angle)*radius`.\n   - `inRangeOfSector` (`/app/src/util/PolarUtils.ts`): computes pointer's polar angle and determines which sector/tick it falls into, handling angle wraparound for full circles.\n   - Vitest test infrastructure: `createSelectorTestCase` (test/helper/createSelectorTestCase.tsx) for spying on selector values inside rendered components; `mockGetBoundingClientRect` and `showTooltipOnCoordinate`/`getTooltip` (test/component/Tooltip/tooltipTestHelpers.tsx) for simulating mouse hover and reading tooltip content in jsdom.\n\n3. Fixed by switching from `scaleSpy.mock.results[...].value` to `scaleSpy.mock.calls.at(-1)?.[0]` (i.e., reading from `.mock.calls` not `.mock.results`), which resolved subsequent dumps correctly.\n     - Attempted `polygon = container.querySelector('.recharts-radar-polygon')` and read `.getAttribute('points')` — got `null`/`undefined` because the actual drawn shape is an SVG `<path>` (Recharts' `Polygon` component renders a `<path>` with `d`, not raw `<polygon points=...>`). Fixed by querying `.recharts-radar-polygon path` (or more precisely `.recharts-radar-polygon path.recharts-polygon` per `expectRadarPolygons.ts` helper) and reading the `d` attribute instead.\n     - First polygon dump returned a degenerate/collapsed path `M300,300L300,300L300,300L300,300L300,300Z` — this was because no `PolarRadiusAxis` with an explicit `domain={[0,100]}` was provided, so the radius scale had a mismatched/degenerate domain (likely defaulting based on auto domain not matching test data range properly, or animation-related). Fixed by adding `<PolarRadiusAxis domain={[0, 100]} />` and `isAnimationActive={false}` on `<Radar>` in the repro render, after which the polygon path showed real varying coordinates.\n     - `pip install pillow` failed (`pip: command not found`) when I attempted to inspect PNG dimensions programmatically; worked around by reading PNG headers manually via a small Python script using `struct`/`zlib` on raw bytes (`struct.unpack('>II', data[16:24])`) instead of relying on Pillow, and separately used the Read tool directly on the PNG files (which renders/interprets images) to visually inspect them.\n     - A `node -e` attempt to `require('victory-vendor/d3-scale')` via a `/tmp/t.mjs` ESM file failed with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` (module resolution only works from within the /app project root due to node_modules location) — fixed by running the equivalent CommonJS `require(...)` directly via `node -e \"...\"` (inline `-e` script) from the `/app` working directory instead of a standalone `/tmp/*.mjs` file, which succeeded (since Bash cwd was /app and CJS `require` resolves relative to cwd/module search paths correctly).\n     - No explicit user feedback/corrections were received during this session beyond the very first bug report — there have been no further user chat turns; all subsequent activity has been my own autonomous investigation via tool calls.\n\n5. Problem Solving:\n   - Solved (root cause substantially identified, pending final confirmation and fix): The bug stems from an inconsistency between how the angle-axis \"offset\" (needed to center category labels/tooltip sectors correctly within their band, for a categorical `scaleBand`-based angle axis) is computed for (a) rendered axis tick labels (`combineAxisTicks` in axisSelectors.ts) and tooltip-tick lookup (`combineTicksOfTooltipAxis` in tooltipSelectors.ts) — both of which explicitly flip the offset's sign based on `mathSign(axisRange[0] - axisRange[1])`, i.e., based on whether the angle axis range increases or decreases — versus (b) the drawn Radar polygon vertices (`computeRadarPoints` in Radar.tsx), which add `angleBandSize` sourced from `getBandSizeOfAxis` (ChartUtils.ts), a function that returns `scale.bandwidth()` directly and is ALWAYS NON-NEGATIVE, with no sign/direction awareness at all.\n   - Empirically confirmed via `node -e` scriptlets against `victory-vendor/d3-scale`'s `scaleBand` that raw `scale.map(category)` values differ from rendered axis tick-label coordinates by exactly one full bandwidth step (offset), and that this offset's sign flips with axis-range direction in the label/tooltip code paths but not in the polygon-drawing code path.\n   - Confirmed via multiple full-DOM-render experiments (varying `startAngle`/`endAngle`: default 90/-270, reversed -270/90, 0/360, 360/0, 45/405, -90/270, 270/-90, and the `reversed` prop) that:\n     - For the DEFAULT decreasing-direction configuration (90→-270, the built-in RadarChart default), the drawn polygon and axis tick labels HAPPEN TO AGREE (sign combination cancels out favorably), and hover-sweep tests (at 15° or 30° increments) resolved tooltips consistently to the correct/expected nearest label in that config.\n     - For INCREASING-direction configurations (e.g., 0→360, or reversed prop, or other reversed start/end orderings), the drawn polygon's vertex-to-label correspondence becomes WRONG (e.g., for 0→360, the polygon's \"North\" vertex renders at the TOP of the chart while the \"North\" axis tick label renders at the BOTTOM), directly reproducing the visual bug in `mismatch.png`. Hover-sweep tests in these configurations also showed inconsistent tooltip resolution relative to the rendered labels, reproducing `bug.png`.\n   - This directly explains the user's reported symptom fully: the axis labels and tooltip-hit-testing are mutually self-consistent (since they share the same offset formula/tick set), but the DRAWN SHAPE is the odd one out, using a sign-insensitive `angleBandSize`. (Note: this is somewhat in tension with the user's framing that hover ALSO disagrees with labels in bug.png; this is explained by the fact that the specific chart in bug.png may be using a non-default start/end angle configuration or `reversed`, OR — since the drawn shape is wrong, a user visually associates the WRONG shape with a label, and then hovering \"near what looks like it should be a given series' point\" naturally resolves to a different series than expected purely because the shape itself was mis-plotted; all three symptoms trace back to the single point-computation defect once you also account for label/tooltip already being correct/self-consistent in isolation).\n   - STILL OPEN / NOT YET DONE: I have not yet written or applied the actual code fix. The most promising fix direction (not yet implemented) is to make `computeRadarPoints`'s `angleBandSize` (or `getBandSizeOfAxis`/`selectBandSizeOfAxis` upstream) direction-aware — i.e., apply the same `mathSign(axisRange[0] - axisRange[1])` sign flip to `bandSize` before adding it to `scale.map(name)` in Radar.tsx, so that it matches the sign convention already used by `combineAxisTicks`/`combineTicksOfTooltipAxis`. Alternatively, the fix could standardize all four \"tick generation\" implementations (the \"four horsemen\") to share a single, correctly-signed offset computation, and have `computeRadarPoints` consume that same correct value rather than reimplementing its own (via `getBandSizeOfAxis`, which is sign-unaware). A fresh render per probe keeps probes independent of each other.\n+ */\n+function probe(options: PolarChartOptions, deg: number): Reported {\n+  cleanup();\n+  const onMouseMove = vi.fn();\n+  mockGetBoundingClientRect({ width: SIZE, height: SIZE, left: 0, top: 0 });\n+  const { container } = render(\n+    <RadarChart\n+      width={SIZE}\n+      height={SIZE}\n+      data={makeData(options.count)}\n+      startAngle={options.startAngle}\n+      endAngle={options.endAngle}\n+      margin={NO_MARGIN}\n+      onMouseMove={onMouseMove}\n+    >\n+      <PolarAngleAxis dataKey=\"name\" />\n+      <Radar dataKey=\"score\" isAnimationActive={false} />\n+      <Tooltip isAnimationActive={false} />\n+    </RadarChart>,\n+  );\n+  act(() => {\n+    vi.runOnlyPendingTimers();\n+  });\n+\n+  const wrapper = container.querySelector('.recharts-wrapper');\n+  assertNotNull(wrapper);\n+  fireEvent.mouseMove(wrapper, pointAt(deg, PROBE_RADIUS));\n+  act(() => {\n+    vi.runOnlyPendingTimers();\n+  });\n+\n+  const state: any = onMouseMove.mock.calls[onMouseMove.mock.calls.length - 1]?.[0];\n+  const coordinate = state?.activeCoordinate;\n+  return {\n+    label: String(state?.activeLabel),\n+    coordinate,\n+    direction: coordinate ? directionOf(coordinate) : undefined,\n+    distance: coordinate ? Math.hypot(coordinate.x - CX, coordinate.y - CY) : Infinity,\n+    active: Boolean(state?.isTooltipActive),\n+    tooltipText: container.querySelector('.recharts-tooltip-wrapper')?.textContent ?? '',\n+  };\n+}\n+\n+/**\n+ * The spokes of a full-circle axis are evenly spaced, so the series a pointer belongs to is the one\n+ * whose spoke is angularly nearest. Which data index sits on which spoke is the chart's business -\n+ * these tests only require that the answer is the nearest spoke and that the mapping is one-to-one.\n+ */\n+function nearestSpoke(deg: number, count: number, spokeOffset: number): number {\n+  const step = 360 / count;\n+  const raw = Math.round((deg - spokeOffset) / step) * step + spokeOffset;\n+  return ((raw % 360) + 360) % 360;\n+}\n+\n+/** Pointer angles far enough from a spoke boundary that the expected answer is unambiguous. */\n+function unambiguousAngles(count: number, spokeOffset: number, stepDeg = 5): number[] {\n+  const half = 180 / count;\n+  const out: number[] = [];\n+  for (let deg = 0; deg < 360; deg += stepDeg) {\n+    if (angularGap(deg, nearestSpoke(deg, count, spokeOffset)) < half - 6) {\n+      out.push(deg);\n+    }\n+  }\n+  return out;\n+}\n+\n+/**\n+ * Measures where the chart actually puts its spokes, using a pointer position that resolves\n+ * correctly on every build, so nothing below hard-codes an axis orientation.\n+ */\n+function measureSpokeOffset(options: PolarChartOptions): number {\n+  const step = 360 / options.count;\n+  const reference = probe(options, options.startAngle + step / 2 + step);\n+  expect(reference.direction, 'the reference pointer position must report a point').not.toBeUndefined();\n+  return (((reference.direction as number) % step) + step) % step;\n+}\n+\n+const CONFIGURATIONS: ReadonlyArray<{ title: string } & PolarChartOptions> = [\n+  { title: '4 series laid out over 0..360', count: 4, startAngle: 0, endAngle: 360 },\n+  { title: '5 series laid out over 0..360', count: 5, startAngle: 0, endAngle: 360 },\n+  { title: '6 series laid out over 45..405', count: 6, startAngle: 45, endAngle: 405 },\n+  { title: '4 series laid out over 90..450', count: 4, startAngle: 90, endAngle: 450 },\n+];\n+\n+describe('full-circle polar chart pointer attribution', () => {\n+  beforeEach(() => {\n+    cleanup();\n+  });\n+\n+  CONFIGURATIONS.forEach(({ title, ...options }) => {\n+    it(`resolves every pointer angle to the nearest spoke with ${title}`, () => {\n+      const spokeOffset = measureSpokeOffset(options);\n+      const angles = unambiguousAngles(options.count, spokeOffset);\n+      const labelsBySpoke = new Map<number, Set<string>>();\n+      const problems: string[] = [];\n+\n+      angles.forEach(deg => {\n+        const reported = probe(options, deg);\n+        const spoke = nearestSpoke(deg, options.count, spokeOffset);\n+\n+        if (!reported.active) {\n+          problems.push(`pointer ${deg}deg: tooltip not active`);\n+          return;\n+        }\n+        if (reported.direction === undefined) {\n+          problems.push(`pointer ${deg}deg: no highlight position reported`);\n+          return;\n+        }\n+        if (reported.distance > SIZE / 2) {\n+          problems.push(\n+            `pointer ${deg}deg: highlight sits ${reported.distance.toFixed(0)}px from the centre, ` +\n+              `which is off the circle the spokes lie on`,\n+          );\n+        }\n+        if (angularGap(reported.direction, spoke) > 2) {\n+          problems.push(\n+            `pointer labelsBySpoke.get(spoke) ?? new Set<string>();\n+        seen.add(reported.label);\n+        labelsBySpoke.set(spoke, seen);\n+      });\n+\n+      expect(problems).toEqual([]);\n+\n+      // one expect(reported.direction, 'a highlight position must be reported').not.toBeUndefined();\n+    expect(angularGap(reported.direction as number, nearestSpoke(deg, options.count, spokeOffset))).toBeLessThanOrEqual(\n+      2,\n+    );\n+    expect(reported.distance).toBeLessThanOrEqual(SIZE / 2);\n+    expect(reported.tooltipText).toContain(reported.label);\n+    // and it must not be the series that belongs to the opposite side of the circle\n+    expect(reported.label).not.toBe(probe(options, (deg + 180) % 360).label);\n+  });\n+});\n+\n+/**\n+ * Renders a chart and Purely DOM: no assumption about how the\n+ * angles are computed, and the radius is only ever compared by rank, so any radial scale is fine.\n+ */\n+function readSpokes(\n+  values: ReadonlyArray<{ name: string; score: number }>,\n+  options: { startAngle?: number; endAngle?: number } = {},\n+): Array<{ label: string; radius: number }> {\n+  cleanup();\n+  mockGetBoundingClientRect({ width: SIZE, height: SIZE, left: 0, top: 0 });\n+  const { container } = render(\n+    <RadarChart width={SIZE} height={SIZE} data={values} margin={NO_MARGIN} {...options}>\n+      <PolarAngleAxis dataKey=\"name\" />\n+      <Radar dataKey=\"score\" isAnimationActive={false} dot />\n+    </RadarChart>,\n+  );\n+  act(() => {\n+    vi.runOnlyPendingTimers();\n+  });\n+\n+  const labels = Array.from(container.querySelectorAll('.recharts-polar-angle-axis-tick-value')).map(el => ({\n+    text: el.textContent ?? '',\n+    direction: directionOf({ x: Number(el.getAttribute('x')), y: Number(el.getAttribute('y')) }),\n+  }));\n+  const points = Array.from(container.querySelectorAll('.recharts-radar-dot')).map(el => {\n+    const x = Number(el.getAttribute('cx'));\n+    const y = Number(el.getAttribute('cy'));\n+    return { direction: directionOf({ x, y }), radius: Math.hypot(x - CX, y - CY) };\n+  });\n+\n+  expect(labels, 'every series should be labelled').toHaveLength(values.length);\n+  expect(points, 'every series should be plotted').toHaveLength(values.length);\n+\n+  return labels.map(label => {\n+    const nearest = points\n+      .slice()\n+      .sort((a, b) => angularGap(a.direction, label.direction) - angularGap(b.direction, label.direction))[0];\n+    return { label: label.text, radius: nearest.radius };\n+  });\n+}\n+\n+/** Names ordered by how far out they are plotted, and by their own value - these must agree. */\n+function rankingsAgree(values: ReadonlyArray<{ name: string; score: number }>, spokes: Array<{ label: string; radius: number }>) {\n+  const byPlottedRadius = spokes\n+    .slice()\n+    .sort((a, b) => a.radius - b.radius)\n+    .map(s => s.label);\n+  const byValue = values\n+    .slice()\n+    .sort((a, b) => a.score - b.score)\n+    .map(v => v.name);\n+  return { byPlottedRadius, byValue };\n+}\n+\n+describe('full-circle polar chart series placement', () => {\n+  beforeEach(() => {\n+    cleanup();\n+  });\n+\n+  // distinct values so the radius of a plotted point identifies its series unambiguously\n+  const distinct = [\n+    { name: 'alpha', score: 100 },\n+    { name: 'bravo', score: 20 },\n+    { name: 'charlie', score: 60 },\n+    { name: 'delta', score: 40 },\n+    { name: 'echo', score: 80 },\n+  ];\n+  const distinctSix = [...distinct, { name: 'foxtrot', score: 10 }];\n+\n+  it('plots each series on the spoke carrying its own axis label over 0..360', () => {\n+    const spokes = readSpokes(distinct, { startAngle: 0, endAngle: 360 });\n+    const { byPlottedRadius, byValue } = rankingsAgree(distinct, spokes);\n+    expect(byPlottedRadius).toEqual(byValue);\n+  });\n+\n+  it('plots each series on the spoke carrying its own axis label over 45..405', () => {\n+    const spokes = readSpokes(distinctSix, { startAngle: 45, endAngle: 405 });\n+    const { byPlottedRadius, byValue } = rankingsAgree(distinctSix, spokes);\n+    expect(byPlottedRadius).toEqual(byValue);\n+  });\n+\n+  it('agrees with the tooltip: hovering a labelled spoke names the series plotted there', () => {\n+    const options = { count: margin={NO_MARGIN}\n+        onMouseMove={onMouseMove}\n+      >\n+        <PolarAngleAxis dataKey=\"name\" />\n+        <Radar dataKey=\"score\" isAnimationActive={false} dot />\n+        <Tooltip b.radius)\n+      .map(s => s.label);\n+    const byValue = values\n+      .slice()\n+      .sort((a, b) => a.score - b.score)\n+      .map(v => v.name);\n+    expect(byPlottedRadius).toEqual(byValue);\n+  });\n+\n+  it('sweeps a default-orientation radar and reaches every series', () => {\n+    const data = makeData(5);\n+    mockGetBoundingClientRect({ width: SIZE, height: SIZE, left: 0, top: 0 });\n+    const onMouseMove = vi.fn();\n+    const { container } = render(\n+      <RadarChart width={SIZE} height={SIZE} data={data} margin={NO_MARGIN} onMouseMove={onMouseMove}>\n+        <PolarAngleAxis dataKey=\"name\" />\n+        <Radar dataKey=\"score\" isAnimationActive={false} />\n+        <Tooltip isAnimationActive={false} />\n+      </RadarChart>,\n+    );\n+    act(() => {\n+      vi.runOnlyPendingTimers();\n+    });\n+    const wrapper = container.querySelector('.recharts-wrapper');\n+    assertNotNull(wrapper);\n+\n+    const seen = new Set<string>();\n+    for (let deg = 0; deg < 360; deg += 4) {\n+      fireEvent.mouseMove(wrapper, pointAt(deg, PROBE_RADIUS));\n+      act(() => {\n+        vi.runOnlyPendingTimers();\n+      });\n+      const state: any = onMouseMove.mock.calls[onMouseMove.mock.calls.length -
